quote: Section 9.4(c) provides: "The limitations set forth in Section 9.4(a) and Section 9.4(b) shall not apply to any claim under Section 9.2(a), or to any claim arising from fraud." Section 9.2(a) covers breaches of Seller's representations and warranties... Seller is liable dollar-for-dollar, without limit, for any inaccurate representation... The Escrow Amount is $1,840,000, but because the cap does not apply to rep breaches, Buyer can pursue Seller directly for any amount above the escrow... Revise § 9.4(c) to: "(c) Exceptions. The limitations set forth in Section 9.4(a) shall not apply to any claim arising from fraud..."
reason: The memo meets all three parts of the criterion. First, it names APA §9.4(c) as removing the 10% cap of §9.4(a). It explains that this applies to all §9.2(a) representation breaches, which it calls the most common claims, and not only fundamental representations. Second, it says this leaves Marrowind with unlimited exposure beyond the $1,840,000 escrow. Third, it recommends narrowing the carve-out to fraud, optionally adding Fundamental Representations.
